Filled dots implement the weak inequalities in the local Definition and carrier Statement; the vertical segment represents {u0} times K_u0 under its natural identification with the interval. The dashed line extends only below the fibre to identify the base coordinate, not as part of K.

The two sloping edges are the graphs of the specified affine functions; the vertical sides lie over the endpoints 0.7 and 4.3 of D. Actual native output shows all four boundary edges and their four corners. Horizontal u and vertical t axes match the Statement coordinate order. The separate horizontal closed bar marked D shares its u-range with K and is an illustrative base interval rather than another fibre.

Proof step 3.1 identifies the section interval and integrates t -> H(u0,t) over it, exactly as the caption states.
